Wells will introduce the legislation tomorrow, then give a major speech at the National Press Club about it. She tells question time Australia already has “one of the most comprehensive online safety frameworks in the world”, but more work is needed. “An independent statutory review has found that it is not able to cope with the growing scale of problems in the online world. Just last week, the AFP commissioner, Krissy Barrett, warned that the police cannot be the only safety net when it comes to the radicalisation of young people online. By the time the AFP is knocking on a door, the harm is already done. She said the digital duty of care would “shift the burden from the shoulders of victims … to the companies that are creating the environments where harms occur.

Photograph: Atef Safadi/EPA Foreign policy New UK sanctions powers will enable action against supporters of illegal Israeli settlements Global human rights commitments adopted by government extend reach to enablers of unlawful activity Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor Wed 14 Oct 2026 12.51 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 13.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The UK is expanding its sanctions powers to freeze assets and target entities enabling illegal Israeli settlements, obstructing humanitarian aid or unlawfully holding prisoners. The statutory instrument introducing the global human rights and international humanitarian law sanctions adds three new grounds to the 2020 regime: serious violations of international humanitarian law, obstruction of humanitarian assistance and serious violations of the right to liberty and security of person. Unlawful settlement activity will be captured through a breach of international humanitarian law, including the Geneva convention on occupation. The Israeli government closed the UK consulate last week in protest, forcing the it to withdraw 21 diplomats and downgrade the consulate to the status of a mission. But the Israeli punishment does not appear to have deterred the UK government. The proposed new powers also extend government reach beyond direct perpetrators of wrongdoing to those who facilitate, incite, promote or support qualifying conduct, provide it with finance, goods or technology, conceal evidence of it or benefit from it. Banks and commercial entities could also fall within this remit as designation only requires reasonable grounds to suspect involvement. Burnham sees sanctions against Israeli settlements as an electoral asset Read more The proposed sanctions measures include asset freezes and prohibitions on making funds or economic resources available, travel bans and director disqualifications. A new urgent procedure will allow ministers to mirror designations already made by the EU, US, Canada or Australia for up to 112 days while a specific separate UK case is prepared. The new global sanctions regime will come into force on Thursday but will need endorsement by MPs and peers within 28 days. The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband , is pushing through the measures at speed because the Israeli government has vowed to press ahead with an E1 settlement containing 1,234 homes in the West Bank – a development that many observers say would sever a contiguous, viable Palestinian state, so making the so-called two-state solution to the Palestinian-Israeli conflict near impossible. The E1 bids close on 19 October but the Israel Land Authority has confirmed that the tender box will not be opened, nor the bids considered, before 19 November, which is after the Israeli election on 27 October. The British Palestinian Project said the Israeli deferral “does not remove the need to deter commitments being made now, since bidders and their backers commit on 19 October, contracts could still be signed before a new Israeli government is formed”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines UK Get the day’s headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morning after newsletter promotion The project welcomed the addition of the right to liberty and security of person in the new laws, saying it opens a route to sanctions for serious arbitrary or unlawful detention, including of Palestinian children, and of those responsible for or enabling it. Save the Children estimated in November 2023 that 10,000 Palestinian children had passed through Israeli military detention over the preceding 20 years. A UN 2026 report on children and armed conflict verified that 981 Palestinian children were detained by Israeli forces in 2025 and 180 of them remained in administrative detention without charge or trial at the year’s end. Will UK sanctions have any impact on Israel’s ‘settler terrorists’ in West Bank? Read more The UK has already applied sanctions designations for restrictions on humanitarian aid in Sudan and South Sudan but this is the first time this general power is being applied as part of a new worldwide regime including Israel. Refusing permits or blocking convoys will be sufficient grounds to apply sanctions, without requiring the obstruction to constitute a formal breach of international humanitarian law – thereby lowering the threshold for action. Separate work is under way by UK officials in conjunction with European partners on how to outlaw British trade with unlawful Israeli settlements. In response to a question from Green politician Marlene Schönberger, the minister of state for culture, Wolfram Weimer , said that "[a]dditional funds for financing beyond the end of 2026 are not available" for the online hub, hosted on the " Archivportal-D " of the German Digital Library. Schönberger, a member of the Bundestag's Committee on Internal Affairs, said she could not understand the decision by the government to cease funding for the portal. "Not even eight months after the launch of the 'Right-Wing Violence' thematic portal, the federal government is now pulling the plug. That is completely incomprehensible," she said. "The federal government must prevent right-wing violence, and where it fails to do so, it must at least acknowledge and document its continuity. It owes that to those affected," she said. The hub was set up to bring together documents held in various archives in one online location. Some 3.7 million households are expected to pay more for electricity, with a rise of some 2% expected. The rise has been cushioned to some extent by coalition's recent agreement to lower the electricity tax rate for 2027 to the European minimum level to protect households and businesses. Gas will become considerably more expensive for some 1.9 million households, with 361 regional utility providers announcing rises of some 14% for December, January and February. "The wholesale prices for gas and electricity, which have risen sharply since the Iran war began in March 2026, are only now starting to have an effect on prices for consumers," Verivox energy expert Thorsten Storck said. In all, 25% of respondents in a YouGov survey wanted aid to Ukraine to be dropped, while 24% were in favor of reducing. Altogether 30% wanted to retain aid at the current level, and 9% felt it should be raised. Eleven percent were undecided on the issue. The survey was conducted between November 13 and 16 on behalf of the newspaper Welt am Sonntag.
